claims_disputed.claim: Incorrect predictions are associated with higher values of all four metrics, and logistic regression confirms comparable negative associations.
claims_disputed.reason: Section IV-D and Table XI fit the four metrics in one model. Cyclomatic complexity and branching factor overlap by definition (§IV-A1). CC counts if/elif/for/while/except plus and/or, starting from 1. BF counts if/for/while. Yet both are reported as independently significant, with tight CIs (DeepSeek CC OR 0.66 [0.57, 0.76], BF OR 0.68 [0.58, 0.79]). The paper gives no correlation matrix or VIF. Taken at face value, the joint coefficients mean one extra `if` (which raises CC and BF together) cuts the odds of a correct answer by about 55% (0.66 x 0.68). The paper never checks this against the band accuracies. Table V is also inconsistent with the definitions as written: the mean CC-minus-BF gap is 0.53-0.97, below the 1 that the stated counting rules imply. Function length is not controlled, even though the paper's own related work (Xie et al., LM-CC) says traditional metrics lose predictive value once length is controlled. The Spearman associations stand as univariate descriptions, but 'logistic regression confirms' is not established.

missed_issues: Complexity band and benchmark source can be partly separated using the paper's own Tables I, III and IV, and the review did not do this. The Low band is entirely HumanEval/MBPP/CRUXEval, and the High band is entirely LeetCode/BigCodeBench-Hard. Within HumanEval/MBPP/CRUXEval, Low to Medium is 93.5% -> 80.6% (79/98) for DeepSeek-Coder-V2 and 87.0% -> 73.5% (72/98) for CodeLlama, so about 13 pp of degradation survives with source held fixed. Within LeetCode/BigCodeBench-Hard, Medium to High is 77.3% (17/22) -> 52.8% for DeepSeek but 50.0% (11/22) -> 47.2% for CodeLlama. That step is split across models and rests on only 22 Medium items. For DeepSeek, the within-source steps (13 and 24 pp) account for most of its 41 pp drop, and the source gap at a fixed Medium band is 3 pp. For CodeLlama, the within-source steps total about 16 of 40 pp, while Medium-band accuracy differs by 24 pp between source groups (73.5% vs 50.0%). So for CodeLlama, most of the headline drop is source difficulty, not structural complexity.

The automatic-task prompt forbids reasoning, and any response containing an explanation is scored incorrect (§IV-C). The paper does not split format violations from wrong values. If models add explanations more often on complex code, part of the High-band drop is a formatting effect rather than a comprehension failure.

The question-type ordering (purpose > variable role > edge case, Table VIII) rests on 20 questions per type. DeepSeek differs by 1-3 items (19/18/16), and the paper runs no test. 'Reflects increasing semantic demand' is an interpretation, not a finding.

In §VI the paper proposes computing complexity before an LLM explains or reviews a function, then requesting test execution or human review above a threshold. That touches untagged P16 (execution verifier) and P19 (human gates) at most as 'introduces'. The gate is never built, so neither pattern gets evidence.
The manual subset's 60 functions and questions were selected and written by the authors with no stated sampling procedure. Kappa 0.86 covers only a 20% double-scored subset, about 12 items per model.
note: My blind pass matches the review on verdict, COI none, rigor, generalizability and relevance. The only score difference is reproducibility (2 vs 1), and the merge keeps 1, which I accept because nothing is released. I agree with all three pattern stances: P43 and P41 neutral, and P17 introduces for the untested complexity-gated verification idea. I lower the logistic-regression claim to weak because CC and BF overlap by definition yet are reported as independently significant in a joint model, with no collinearity check and no length control. Re-deriving within-source accuracies from Tables I, III and IV gives a 13 pp Low-to-Medium drop for both models with benchmark source held fixed. Beyond that, the complexity effect survives source control for DeepSeek but mostly does not for CodeLlama. For the team this is weak support for a deterministic complexity trigger on agent explanations, not a measure of how large the risk is.
